llm_evaluation.realism: The samples are highly realistic, reflecting common spear phishing tactics such as domain impersonation, use of recently registered domains with privacy protection, targeted social engineering messages, and inclusion of technical details like email headers, SMTP logs, and domain registration info. The scenarios cover a variety of targets and attack vectors (links, attachments, calendar invites) consistent with real-world spear phishing campaigns. The use of plausible sender names, corporate roles, and contextual urgency enhances believability. The inclusion of DKIM signatures, IP addresses, and detailed email metadata further adds to authenticity.
llm_evaluation.consistency: The dataset is consistent in structure and schema across all samples, with each entry containing scenario descriptions, detailed technical data (email headers, body, SMTP logs, domain registration, malicious URLs/attachments), indicators, detection methods, and relevant MITRE techniques. The formatting of fields such as dates, IP addresses, and hashes is uniform. All samples include appropriate MIME types and email content types matching the described attack vector. The indicators and detection methods logically align with the scenario and technical data provided.
suggestions: Include more variation in email client user-agent strings and mailer headers to reflect diverse real-world environments.
Add more explicit references to social engineering elements in the email body text, such as personalized greetings using victim-specific data or references to recent events.
Incorporate some examples with failed or missing DKIM/SPF/DMARC to reflect common misconfigurations or spoofing attempts.
Expand on the SMTP transaction logs to include more realistic timestamps and possible error or retry messages to simulate real mail server behavior.
For the URL obfuscation field, consider adding examples of homograph attacks or use of Unicode characters to increase complexity.
Include some samples with multi-part email bodies containing both plain text and HTML versions for completeness.
Add more diversity in domain registrars and registrant privacy services to avoid repetitive patterns.
Consider including examples where the malicious URL redirects multiple times or uses IP-based URLs to simulate advanced obfuscation.
Provide more detailed attachment metadata such as file size, creation/modification dates, and embedded macro behavior descriptions.
Introduce some samples with embedded images or tracking pixels to reflect common phishing techniques.
